A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same FUSE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices can be reliably matched despite the changed title, format and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original news-evolution simulations, ablations, intervention experiments and comparisons between LLM and human evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original simulation and evaluation results and additionally reports agreement among human annotators.

M1.justification: The PRA/NES framework, four agent roles, memory and decision procedures, intervention mechanism and prompts are retained. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same five news topics, three network types, spread modes, personality conditions and intervention scenarios. V2's newly stated 120-item collection remains within this coverage; the illustrative news items also match.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o-mini, while the backbone comparison retains GPT-4 and GPT-4o-mini. Ablation and intervention controls also match. FPS and TED appear in related-work discussion, without new evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated simulation size, model choices, scoring rules and intervention timing match. V2 specifies corpus and annotation sample counts that v1 left unspecified; these disclosures do not establish a revision to the existing evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix D extends human-evaluation validation with an inter-annotator agreement check. The memory and role ablations, intervention analyses, case studies, topic/network analyses and backbone robustness experiments are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly describes Table 1's existing bold entries as significant under a t-test with p<0.01 and reports Fleiss' kappa in Appendix D. This adds statistical reporting, but no additional simulation runs or seeds are documented, and the t-test design remains unspecified.

E6.justification: V2 adds Fleiss' kappa=0.79 and a brief statement of consistent results for the 120-item news collection. Tables 1 and 2, the 73% fake-news recovery claim, and the matched simulation, ablation and intervention plots retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and the clustering, power-law, binomial and Poisson definitions are retained. The network mathematics moves from v1 Appendix G to v2 Appendix I; no new proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The central claims remain FUSE's simulation of true-to-fake news evolution, FUSE-EVAL, alignment with observed patterns and the benefits of early intervention. The contribution list is consolidated, and extensibility was already claimed in v1 Appendix F.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive limitations discussion absent from v1: insufficient datasets capturing news evolution, omitted political/ideological/crisis contexts, incomplete evaluation dimensions and biases from LLM simulation and evaluation. These substantially broaden the qualifications concerning validation and real-world applicability.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code/data release; v2 supplies a concrete anonymous code URL in Appendix C. V2 also specifies 120 news items reportedly published after the model's training cutoff and three Ph.D. annotators evaluating 50 items, improving documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: V2 removes the dedicated survey of epidemic, point-process and diffusion models and substantially prunes general agent-application literature. It foregrounds the previously cited FPS, adds TED and newer agent work, and adds supporting references on personality, rumor networks and annotator agreement.

P1.justification: The title and author block change, and the abstract, introduction, methods and discussion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Related work and contributions are reorganized, algorithm and implementation material move into appendices, and a limitations section is introduced.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document and regroups existing figures: v1 Figure 3(a) and Figure 4 become v2 Figure 3, while v1 Figure 3(b–d) becomes v2 Figure 4. Tables and algorithm placement change, and Figure 5 relabels PS as PD without changing its percentages.

improvement.justification: The annotation details, agreement result, code-access reference and explicit limitations make v2 more transparent and better qualify its conclusions. These gains outweigh the reduced background coverage, although the new Table 1 significance claim lacks test-design detail and the central empirical evidence remains largely unchanged. The overall improvement is useful but limited.
